name: Lettuce (Loose Leaf)
description: A fast-growing, cool-season crop. Loose-leaf varieties allow for a continuous 'cut-and-come-again' harvest.
tips: Provide afternoon shade in warmer weather to prevent bolting (going to seed) and extend the harvest season.
succession: Essential for a steady supply. Sow new seeds every 2 weeks throughout the growing season.
yield: Continuous harvest of outer leaves. 2-3 plants per person is usually sufficient at any one time.

soil.type: Loose, well-drained soil with plenty of organic matter.
soil.notes: Lettuce has shallow roots, so consistent moisture near the surface is crucial. Benefits from a light feeding of nitrogen.

temperature.notes: A cool-season crop. Will bolt and become bitter in hot weather (above 80°F). Appreciates afternoon shade.

environmentalAlerts.message: Lettuce can tolerate a light frost, but cover if a hard freeze is expected to extend the harvest.

storage.notes: Wash and dry leaves thoroughly. Store in a plastic bag or container with a paper towel to absorb excess moisture.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over a week to prevent shock.

careTasks.name: Thin direct-sown seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin seedlings to 6-8 inches apart. The thinnings are edible and can be used in salads.

careTasks.name: Harvest outer leaves
careTasks.description: Harvest the larger, outer leaves at the base of the plant, leaving the central leaves to continue growing. This 'cut-and-come-again' method prolongs the harvest.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Lettuce has shallow roots and needs consistent, light watering. Water when the top inch of soil is dry to keep it from becoming bitter. Avoid waterlogging the soil.

name: Spinach
description: A very cold-hardy and nutritious, cool-season crop. Best planted in early spring and/or fall.
tips: Spinach bolts very quickly in response to heat and long day length. Choose bolt-resistant varieties for later plantings.
succession: Sow seeds every 2 weeks in early spring and again in late summer for a fall crop. Avoid sowing in late spring as heat causes rapid bolting.
yield: Continuous harvest of leaves. A 10-foot row can provide plenty for a family.

soil.notes: Prefers neutral to slightly alkaline soil. Requires ample nitrogen for lush, dark green leaves. Amend with compost or aged manure.

temperature.notes: Very cold-hardy and can be planted as soon as soil is workable in spring. Bolts quickly in heat.

environmentalAlerts.message: Spinach is very frost tolerant and flavor can improve with a light frost. Cover only if a hard freeze is expected.

storage.notes: Store unwashed in a plastic bag in the crisper. Wash just before use to prevent premature decay. Also freezes well after blanching.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Thin seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin seedlings to 4-6 inches apart to allow plants to fully develop without competition.

careTasks.name: Harvest outer leaves
careTasks.description: Once leaves are 3-4 inches long, begin harvesting the outer leaves, allowing the inner leaves to continue growing.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Spinach needs consistent moisture for tender leaves and to prevent bolting. Water when the top inch of soil is dry. Mulch can help retain moisture.

name: Kale
description: A hardy and productive cool-season green from the cabbage family. Its flavor famously gets sweeter after a light frost.
tips: Harvest outer leaves from the bottom up to allow the center of the plant to keep producing new leaves. Very cold tolerant and can often be harvested into winter.
succession: Not usually necessary as one planting provides a long harvest. Can plant a second crop in mid-summer for a fall/winter harvest.
yield: Continuous harvest of leaves over many months.

soil.notes: Tolerant of average soils but thrives with compost. Benefits from a side-dressing of nitrogen mid-season for best production.

temperature.notes: Extremely hardy. Flavor is improved and sweetened by a light frost. Tolerates summer heat better than many other greens.

environmentalAlerts.message: Kale is very frost tolerant and flavor improves with a light frost. Cover only if a severe freeze is expected.

storage.notes: Store in a plastic bag in the crisper drawer. For best results, wash, dry, and then store. Can be blanched and frozen for long-term storage.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over a week to prevent shock.

careTasks.name: Monitor for cabbage worms
careTasks.description: Inspect leaves, especially the undersides, for small green caterpillars and their droppings. Use row covers or hand-pick pests.

careTasks.name: Begin harvesting outer leaves
careTasks.description: Harvest the lowest, outermost leaves when they reach a usable size. This encourages new growth from the top-center of the plant.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Kale produces best with consistent moisture. Water when the top inch of soil feels dry. Mulching helps keep the soil cool and moist.

name: Swiss Chard
description: A beautiful and productive leafy green from the beet family, grown for its tender leaves and crisp stems. More heat-tolerant than spinach.
tips: Harvest outer leaves regularly to encourage continued growth. Both the leaves and the colorful stems are edible.
succession: Not necessary. One planting provides a continuous harvest from late spring until a hard frost.
yield: Continuous harvest of leaves and stems all season long.

soil.type: Well-drained soil rich in organic matter.
soil.notes: Tolerant of average soil but produces best with regular moisture and fertility. Amend with compost before planting.

temperature.notes: More heat-tolerant than spinach and will continue to produce through the summer in most climates. Also tolerates light frost.

environmentalAlerts.message: Swiss Chard can tolerate a light frost, but cover if a hard freeze is expected to extend the harvest.

storage.notes: Store unwashed in a plastic bag in the crisper. Stems and leaves can be stored separately if desired.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over a week to prevent shock.

careTasks.name: Thin direct-sown seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin seedlings to 6-8 inches apart. Use the tender thinnings in salads.

careTasks.name: Monitor for leaf miners
careTasks.description: Inspect leaves for twisting trails, a sign of leaf miners. Remove and destroy affected leaves immediately to prevent spread.

careTasks.name: Begin harvesting outer leaves
careTasks.description: Cut the outer leaves at the base of the plant, leaving the inner leaves to grow. This provides a continuous harvest.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Swiss chard needs consistent moisture for tender leaves and stems. Water when the top inch of soil feels dry.

name: Arugula
description: A fast-growing, cool-season green with a peppery, nutty flavor. It bolts very quickly in warm weather.
tips: Harvest leaves when they are young and tender for the mildest flavor. The flowers are also edible and have a similar peppery taste.
succession: Sow every 2-3 weeks for a continuous supply. It grows so fast that succession planting is key to having it all season.
yield: Continuous harvest of leaves. A small patch is often enough due to its fast growth.

soil.notes: Does not require overly rich soil. Consistent water is more important to prevent bolting and keep flavor mild.

temperature.notes: A cool-season green that bolts extremely quickly in heat, making the leaves very peppery or bitter. Provide afternoon shade in warm weather.

environmentalAlerts.message: Arugula can tolerate a light frost, but cover if a hard freeze is expected to extend the harvest.

storage.notes: Very perishable. Wash, dry thoroughly, and store in a plastic bag with a paper towel to absorb moisture.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Thin seedlings
careTasks.description: Thin seedlings to 4-6 inches apart for best growth. Use the thinnings as microgreens.

careTasks.name: Monitor for flea beetles
careTasks.description: Check leaves for tiny 'shot-hole' damage from flea beetles. Use row covers on young plants for protection.

careTasks.name: Begin harvesting leaves
careTasks.description: Harvest outer leaves when they are 2-3 inches long. Regular harvesting can delay bolting.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Consistent watering is key for mild-tasting arugula and to prevent bolting. Water when the top inch of soil feels dry.

name: Collard Greens
description: A large-leafed, very cold-hardy green from the cabbage family, popular in Southern US cooking. Flavor improves after frost.
tips: Harvest outer leaves from the bottom up to allow the plant to grow and produce for a long period. Can produce well into the winter in mild climates.
succession: Not usually necessary as plants are very productive. A second planting in mid-summer can provide a tender fall crop.
yield: Continuous harvest of leaves. A few plants can provide a large harvest over a long season.

soil.notes: Benefits from soil rich in organic matter and a consistent supply of nitrogen to produce large, tender leaves.

temperature.notes: Very heat and cold tolerant. Flavor is significantly improved and sweetened after a couple of light frosts.

environmentalAlerts.message: Collard Greens are very frost tolerant and flavor improves with a light frost. Cover only if a severe freeze is expected.

storage.notes: Store unwashed in a plastic bag in the crisper. Can be blanched and frozen for long-term preservation.

careTasks.name: Care for Seedlings
careTasks.description: Keep the soil consistently moist, like a damp sponge, to help seeds germinate. Avoid letting the soil dry out completely.

careTasks.name: Begin hardening off seedlings
careTasks.description: Gradually expose seedlings to outdoor conditions over a week to prevent shock.

careTasks.name: Monitor for cabbage worms and aphids
careTasks.description: Check leaves for caterpillars and clusters of aphids. Hand-pick or use insecticidal soap as needed.

careTasks.name: Begin harvesting outer leaves
careTasks.description: Harvest the lower leaves first, working your way up the stalk. This allows the plant to continue producing from its growing tip.

careTasks.name: Watering
careTasks.description: Collards are best when they grow fast and stay hydrated. Water when the top inch of soil feels dry to keep leaves from getting tough.
